title: How to get an Apple student discount at Apple’s Education Store and how much you can save
content:
Macworld





Apple rarely discounts its products for general consumers, but eligible students, parents and teachers can save by shopping at the Apple Education Store. The dedicated storefront offers year-round discounts of around 5% to 15% on selected MacBooks, Macs, iPads and some Apple Watch models.
Education pricing is available to university students, parents buying on behalf of students, and staff at eligible educational institutions. Shoppers may need to verify their eligibility, and Apple limits the number of discounted products that can be purchased each year.
Students can save even more during Apple’s annual Back to School promotion. The 2026 offer is currently live in the U.S, U.K. and Europe. and adds a free Gift Card worth up to $150/£120/€120 with qualifying purchases until September 24 in the U.S. and October 22 in the U.K and Europe. These savings are particularly valuable following Apple’s June 25, 2026 Mac and iPad price increases, which raised prices by as much as £500 on some products.
This guide explains who qualifies for Apple Education pricing, how much you can save, the best time to buy, and how to maximise your savings through seasonal promotions and other offers.


How to find the Apple Education Store
If you qualify as a student you can shop at Apple’s Education Store, where you can find discounted pricing, and occasionally promotions. Click on the links below to go straight to the store where you are:
Apple’s U.S. Education Store
Apple’s U.K. Education Store 
Apple’s Canada Education Store
Apple’s Australian Education Store


						

							


What can you save with the Apple Education Store?

				
					

				
			
Apple’s Education  Store.

Foundry




Apple Education pricing offers year-round discounts on selected Macs, iPads and accessories for eligible students, parents, teachers and education staff.
Savings vary by product and region, but Macs usually receive the biggest discounts. MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac mini models are commonly reduced by between $100 and $200, while selected iPads can be up to $100 cheaper through the Education Store. In May 2026 Apple added Apple Watch education pricing for students with discounts of up to $130. Smaller discounts may also be available on accessories such as the Apple Pencil and Magic Keyboard.
Typical savings include:
$200/£200 off an MacBook Pro
$100/£100 off an MacBook Air
$100/£100 off an iPad Pro
$50/£50 off an iPad Air
$80/£80 off an Apple Watch Ultra 3
$40/£40 off an Apple Watch Series 11 
£10/$10 off the Apple Pencil Pro
£10/$10 off the standard Apple Pencil
Savings are larger on higher-spec configurations. 
You can compare all the student savings for Mac, iPad student discounts, and Apple Watch student savings in our tables further down the page.
Other savings
Apple also offers discounted services and software for students: 
Apple Music & Apple TV: Eligible students can subscribe to Apple Music at $6.99/£5.99 a month, rather than the standard $11.99/£11.99. Apple TV+ is also included in that subscription for as long as you are a student. Here’s how students can get Apple Music for almost half price. 
Apple’s Pro Apps Bundle for Education: This bundle is available only to students during the checkout process, and costs just $199.99/£199.99. More information about how to redeem it here. It includes:
Final Cut Pro – professional video editing software
Logic Pro – music production and audio editing
Motion – motion graphics and visual effects
Compressor – video encoding and export tools
MainStage – live performance software for musicians
Creator Studio: Alternatively you can subscribe to the Creator Studio – which is free for the first three months. The Apple Creator Studio education price is $2.99/£2.99 a month or $29/£29 a year. For non students, Creator Studio is available for a recurring subscription at $12.99/£12.99 a month, $129/£129 a year. Creator Studio adds Pixelmator Pro to the apps available in the Pro Apps Bundle, as well as premium features for:
Keynote
Pages
Numbers
Freeform
Adobe and Microsoft also offer student discounts.


						

							


Who can use Apple’s Education Store
To access these savings, you must be a higher education student, a parent buying for one, or an educator/staff member at any grade level.
Higher Education Students: Full-time students currently enrolled in a college or university (18+).
Parents: Those purchasing on behalf of a student currently in higher education.
Educators and Staff: All teachers and faculty for K-12 or higher education, as well as administrative and other staff members working at an educational institution.
Homeschool Parents: Parents who are homeschooling their children are also eligible, though they may need to provide additional documentation for verification.
It is important to note that standard education pricing is generally not available for school-age children (K-12 students) or their parents, unless the parent is a teacher or a homeschooler.


						

							







How to shop at Apple’s Education Store 

				
					

				
			
Get Education Savings from Apple.

Foundry




With your status verified, you can shop at the Education Store for your country. 
Apple’s U.S. Education Store
Apple’s U.K. Education Store
Apple’s Canada Education Store
Apple’s Australian Education Store
Here you will see special pricing for Mac, iPad, Apple Watch and certain accessories. Apple indicates education savings for products where applicable. 
Select the product and configuration you wish to purchase. 
Add accessories of software if required.
If you have one you can add a trade-in device and get even more money off. 
Choose whether to add AppleCare+, which also includes an education saving. (£179 3 years/£69.99/yr)
Verify eligibility if prompted
Complete checkout
Those buying on behalf of a school or university, rather than for individual use, need to sign in their institution’s account at Apple’s Store for Education Institutions. 
Visit the U.S. Apple Store for Education Institutions (if that link doesn’t work), the U.K. Apple Store for Education Institutions (if that link doesn’t work), or the Canadian or Australian equivalent and search for your Educational Institution. If your institution is found you will be able to sign in to access your institution’s store.


						

							


How to verify student status to use Apple’s Education Store

				
					

				
			
Verify your student status at UNiDAYS.

Foundry




Before gaining access to discounted pricing on Apple’s Education Store, students, teachers and education staff must verify their eligibility.
In many regions, Apple requires shoppers to confirm their educational status through the third-party verification service UNiDAYS. UNiDAYS verification was already mandatory in the U.K., but Apple expanded the requirement in May 2026 to additional regions including the United States, Australia, Canada, Hong Kong, Turkey and Chile as part of a stricter verification process. 
Visit the UNiDAYS website.
Create a UNiDAYS account.
Provide details of your college or university.
Provide your student email address.
UNiDAYS can usually verify student status by confirming your email address, but if that isn’t successful you may need to provide your student ID or other evidence.


						

							


Other ways students can save
There are several ways to save beyond the standard Education Store pricing. Additional savings can often be found through Apple Certified Refurbished products, trade-in programmes and discounts from third-party retailers such as Amazon and Best Buy.
Apple Certified Refurbished Store
Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store is one of the few places where the company directly reduces prices on its hardware. Refurbished devices undergo extensive testing, are restored to “like-new” condition, and include a one-year warranty with the option to add AppleCare coverage.
Discounts typically range from 15% to 30% compared with the original retail price. Recent examples have included savings of around $200 to $250 on refurbished M4 iMac models in the US store. 
See Best place to buy a refurbished MacBook or Mac for more information.




Third-Party Reseller Deals
Resellers often provide deeper discounts than Apple, especially during major shopping events like Black Friday, Amazon Prime Day, or clearance periods.
In the U.S., check Amazon, B&H Photo, Best Buy, and Walmart.
In the U.K., Amazon, Currys, John Lewis, and KRCS are recommended.
Check our Best Apple Deals collection for the best deals we’ve seen, including the best iPad deals, and the best MacBook Pro, MacBook Air and MacBook Neo deals, updated regularly. We often see much bigger savings than you can get in the education store. 
Trade-In Programs
Apple and various resellers allow you to trade in old devices for credit toward a new purchase. This effectively lowers the out-of-pocket cost and is a convenient way to dispose of older hardware responsibly.
Read: How to sell or trade-in your old Mac and save on a new one.

 FAQ 


1.
Are there purchase limits?
Yes. Student shoppers are subject to annual purchase limits:
Apple limits the number of discounted items you can buy from the Education Store each year:
One desktop Mac.
One Mac laptop.
Two iPads. 
One Apple Watch. 
Two accessories.





2.
When is the best time to shop at the Apple Education Store?
The best time to buy is during Apple’s annual Back to School promotion, which usually runs between June and September in the Northern Hemisphere, and January to March in countries such as Australia and New Zealand.
During the promotion, Apple adds extra incentives on top of its standard education discounts, making it one of the cheapest times of year to buy directly from Apple.
Recent Back to School offers have included:
Free AirPods or Apple Pencil models with qualifying Macs or iPads
Discounted upgrades to AirPods Pro
Savings on accessories such as the Magic Keyboard, Magic Mouse and Magic Trackpad
Gift cards with eligible purchases in selected regions





3.
Who qualifies for Apple Education pricing?
In the U.S., Apple says the following groups are eligible for Education Store discounts:
K–12 employees, including homeschool teachers
School board members and some PTA/PTO officers
University and college students, including those accepted into higher education
Parents buying on behalf of eligible higher education students
Faculty and staff at higher education institutions
Apple has similar eligibility rules in the U.K., where discounts are available to:
Employees of public and private educational institutions
Students attending or accepted into post-secondary education
Parents purchasing for eligible post-secondary students
Apple may request proof of eligibility during or after purchase.





4.
Can parents buy through the Apple Education Store for their children?
Parents can purchase products through the Apple Education Store for their children, but only if the child is a student in higher education (college or university). Apple’s education pricing is not available to parents buying for children in K-12 (grade school, middle school, or high school), unless the parent is a teacher or a home educator.





5.
Does Apple offer student discounts on AppleCare?
Apple does not offer separate student discounts on AppleCare+, but education customers can still add AppleCare+ to their Apple Education Store purchases.





6.
Can you pay monthly or use Apple finance plans on the Apple Education Store?
Yes. In most countries, Apple allows customers to use monthly payment plans and financing options when buying through the Apple Education Store.





7.
How often does Apple change Education Store pricing?
The discounts are typically updated when Apple introduces new products. The percentage saving is usually the same: between 5% and 15% off.





8.
What happens if Apple asks for proof of eligibility after purchase?
You may need to provide the following, in addition to being verified via UNIDAYS:
A student ID card
University acceptance or enrolment documents
A school or university email address
Without this your order may be cancelled.

title: iPhone 17 Remains World's Best Selling Smartphone
content:
The iPhone 17 retained its position as the world's best selling smartphone in the second quarter of 2026, according to Counterpoint Research, with the iPhone 17 Pro Max and ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ holding the next two spots on the firm's quarterly ranking.


Data from Counterpoint's Global Handset Model Sales Tracker places the standard ‌iPhone 17‌ at 6% of global smartphone unit sales for the second quarter, building on the top spot it already held in the first quarter. Apple and Samsung filled all ten of the top spots, with a combined 26% share of worldwide unit sales that was two points higher than a year earlier.

Counterpoint tied the growth to regional strength outside Apple's usual core markets, with gains in India, Japan, and the Middle East and Africa, plus a near doubling of sales in South Korea. 

The base iPhone 17 model remained the best selling smartphone during the quarter, supported by significant upgrades that narrowed the gap with the Pro models. Meanwhile, strong premium demand drove the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max sales, aided by trade in programs, promotions, and accessible financing options that improved affordability.


Rising smartphone prices across the industry also nudged buyers toward more expensive pricing tiers generally, which largely worked in Apple's favor given its lineup skews upmarket already.



iPhone 17e took seventh place following its refresh that added MagSafe and increased storage for the same price, boosted by compelling carrier deals in the U.S. and Japan. The iPhone 16 rounded out the list at number ten, leaving Apple with five of the ten slots, which is the same count and nearly the same positions Apple held a year earlier with the ‌iPhone 16‌ lineup and iPhone 15.

Samsung's best performer was the Galaxy S26 Ultra in fourth place, which is the first time that Samsung's top tier device has outsold every other Android phone in the second quarter. This is said to partly be a reflection of Samsung steering more marketing spend toward its flagship models to protect margins as costs climb. Samsung's cheaper Galaxy A phones also remained competitive further down the market.

title: Apple Wallet Driver's License Feature Just Launched in Virginia
content:
Starting today, Virginia residents can add a digital version of their driver's license to the Apple Wallet app on the iPhone and Apple Watch. The digital ID can be used to display proof of identity or age at TSA checkpoints in select airports, at select businesses, and in select apps, but the number of places where it is accepted is still quite limited.


Virginia is the 15th state to implement support for Apple Wallet IDs in the U.S., joining Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Georgia, Hawaii, Illinois, Iowa, Maryland, Montana, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, and West Virginia. The feature is also available in Puerto Rico, and it works with Japan's My Number Card.

Apple has been preparing for the feature to go live in North Carolina, Oklahoma, and Utah in the coming months, and years ago it announced that Connecticut, Kentucky, and Mississippi were committed to launching the feature at some point.

To set up the feature, open the Wallet app on the iPhone and tap on the plus sign in the top-right corner. Next, tap on Driver's License and ID Cards, select Virginia from the list, and follow the on-screen steps to complete the process. Then, you can present your digital ID where it is accepted without handing over your device.


You can present an Apple Wallet ID where accepted by simply tapping your iPhone or Apple Watch on an identity reader. Then, you will be able to view the specific information being requested by the TSA or business. Only after authorizing with Face ID or Touch ID is the requested identity information released from your device.

As mentioned, you do not need to unlock, show, or hand over your device to present an Apple Wallet ID in person, ensuring user privacy.

Apple Wallet IDs are generally not accepted by law enforcement, so carrying a physical ID is still legally required for traffic stops. In addition, the number of businesses that accept Apple Wallet IDs is still quite small. At least for now, Apple Wallet IDs are designed to be a convenient alternative where they are accepted.

title: Best Mac 2026: Every Apple Mac and MacBook compared
content:
Macworld






Which Mac is best for you? 
Whether you want everyday portability, professional creative power, desktop performance, or budget-friendly computing, Apple’s lineup has a Mac that fits. For $699 you can own a MacBook Neo, which is Apple’s most affordable laptop. Spend a little more and the MacBook Air excels at everyday work and battery life, while the MacBook Pro lineup delivers the extra power required by demanding professional workloads. If you prefer a desktop, the iMac is a great all-in-one option for the home, while Mac mini offers good value if you don’t need portability and already have a display and accessories. At the top end, the Mac Studio is built for intensive professional workloads, including demanding creative work and AI development.
Choosing the best Mac in 2026 isn’t simply about buying the newest model; it’s about finding the Mac that best matches what you need from a computer. Apple’s lineup ranges from ultraportable MacBooks to powerful desktop Macs, with options for students, everyday users, creatives and professionals.
In this Mac buying guide, we cover everything you need to know about the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, Mac mini, iMac and Mac Studio, including the differences in size, specs, features and price. We’ll help you decide which Mac and configuration offers the right balance of value, performance and portability for you.
Best Mac 2026: Mac & MacBook Buyers Guide
Our top Mac for most people in 2026 is the MacBook Air. It offers an excellent combination of performance, portability and value in a compact package that will suit the typical Mac user.
If you need more power, we recommend the MacBook Pro, which delivers high-end performance in a portable form. At the other end of the price range, the new MacBook Neo starts at $699/£699 and is Apple’s most affordable Mac laptop.
If you don’t need a laptop, Apple also has some excellent desktop options. The Mac Studio offers exceptional performance for the money and can save thousands compared with a similarly specified Mac laptop, while the Mac mini is Apple’s cheapest desktop Mac, starting at $899/£899.
Below, we take you through every Mac currently available from Apple, explaining who each model is best suited to and what you should consider when choosing a configuration. You’ll also find live prices to help you find the best deal today. For more help choosing between Apple’s laptops, see our MacBook comparison.
Price increases June 2026
In June 2026, Apple increased prices significantly across several product lines including Macs, iPads, the Apple TV 4K, and HomePod models, citing an unprecedented rise in component costs. 
The company stated it had “never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly” and that it had shielded customers from these increases for as long as possible before finally raising prices. 
For Macs, prices increased from $100/£100 to $500/£500 depending on the model.

Who’s it for? It’s perfect for students and everyday users who want a lightweight laptop that’s easy to carry, and powerful enough for working, studying, browsing, and doing light creative work. If you want a larger screen there is a 15-inch MacBook Air, which we discuss below. 
How much does the 13-inch MacBook Air cost? The entry-level 13-inch M5 MacBook Air costs from $1,299/£1,299, that’s up $200/£200 from the launch price of $1,099/£1,099. You can create build-to-order models with more memory (up to 32GB) or storage (up to 4TB).
What are the specifications? The standard specs for the M5 MacBook Air offer an improvement compared to the previous generation. The MacBook Air now ships with 512GB SSD as standard.

How do I connect stuff? The M5 MacBook Air models supports Thunderbolt 4, which means that they can support a dual monitor set up. If you want to connect USB-A devices, you need either a USB-C to USB-A adapter, like Apple’s $19 / £19 one, or a USB-C hub that has USB-A ports. In the U.K. and Europe Apple has stopped including a Power Adapter in the box, so you will need to buy one separately. See our round-up of the best USB-C hubs and adapters.
The 2026 MacBook Air offers Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) for connecting to a network. It also provides built-in Bluetooth (6) for wirelessly connecting a mouse or other peripherals. If you want to connect to an ethernet network, you need an adapter.
How fast is it? In our tests the M5 saw consistent gains over the M4 in the previous generation, as you can see in our Mac processor benchmarks. In some benchmarks the M3 even beats the M1 Ultra. If you are upgrading from an old Mac – especially if it is one with an Intel chip – you will see a huge difference.
Any other considerations? The MacBook Air should be more than fast enough for general-purpose use. The only issue is that, because it doesn’t have an internal fan, it may slow down during long processing sessions to keep cool. So if you are likely to be video editing or compiling code the MacBook Pro with its fan is a better choice. Also note that it’s impossible to upgrade the storage or memory after purchase, so you should buy the model with the largest amount of storage and memory you can afford or invest in external storage. 
Why we recommend the 13-inch MacBook Air: The MacBook Air is a great choice for someone who does general-purpose work and moves around a lot, such as a student or a self-employed person.

How fast is it? MacBook Neo uses the A18 Pro chip that first appeared in the iPhone 16 Pro. Our tests and benchmarks of that chip indicate that it offers similar performance to the M1. It is suitable for everyday tasks like web browsing, streaming, and office apps.
Any other considerations? To get to the low price Apple has made several trade-offs. The MacBook Neo lacks Thunderbolt and MagSafe support, there is no keyboard backlight and no Touch ID on the base model, and RAM is limited to 8GB with no option to increase that to 16GB.
Why we recommend the MacBook Neo: This is the most affordable way to own a Mac laptop – unless you buy a used or refurbished model. If you don’t need pro-level performance it’s a very compelling entry-point into Apple’s ecosystem.

Any other considerations? The Air doesn’t have a fan to keep the computer cool, so it may throttle down its speed during long processing sessions, such as video editing or compiling code. In some of our tests the M5 beat the M1 Ultra, which shows the progress Apple has made with its silicon over the past few years. The MacBook Air matches the specs of the M5 MacBook Pro, but the Pro outperforms the Air due to the inclusion of a fan for cooling (the MacBook Air doesn’t have the space for this). If you need it, more power is available from the MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or Max.
Any other considerations? Our advice is to max out the RAM (aka Unified Memory) and storage when you buy a Mac because you can’t update it later on.

Who’s it for? The iMac is great for both novices and demanding users. It’s ideal for someone who needs to buy a complete computer setup (keyboard, mouse or trackpad, and display) and wants to maximize workspace efficiency. The 24-inch iMac is a design icon that will look great in any office.
How much does the iMac cost? Following the June price hikes, the three standard configurations start at $1,499/£1,499 (up from $1,299/£1,299) for the entry-level model, and $1,699/£1,699 (up from $1,499/£1,499) for the mid-range.
What are the specifications? The 24-inch iMac still uses Apple’s M4 chip. Compared to other Macs, there is half the storage as standard, at 256GB. There are several configurations available as well as build-to-order options:
Apple M4, 8-core CPU, 8-core GPU, 16GB memory, 256GB SSD, two Thunderbolt 4 ports, $1,499/£1,499.
Apple M4, 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB memory, 256GB SSD, four Thunderbolt 4 ports, $1,699/£1,699.
Apple M4, 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB memory, 512GB SSD, four Thunderbolt 4 ports, $1,899/£1,899.
Apple M4, 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 24GB memory, 512GB SSD, four Thunderbolt 4 ports, $2,099/£2,099.
Additional options: 32GB memory; up to 2TB storage
What are the display specifications? The 24-inch 4.5K Retina display has 11.3 million pixels and supports the P3 wide color gamut, over a billion colors, 500 nits of brightness, and True Tone. Apple treats the display with an anti-reflective coating to help with readability. The display hasn’t changed since the M1 model launched.
How do I connect stuff? The $1,499 24-inch iMac 24 has two Thunderbolt 4 ports that also work with USB-C devices. The $1,699 and $1,899 iMacs have four Thunderbolt 4 ports (the previous generation had two Thunderbolt/USB 4 and two USB 3 ports). If you have a USB-A device, you need to buy an adapter, such as Apple’s ($19 / £19). If you have multiple USB-A devices and other items, consider a Thunderbolt hub. The 24-inch iMac also has a headphone jack on the side.
Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 are built-in. Apple doesn’t put a gigabit ethernet port on the 24-inch iMac—instead, it’s on the power adapter. But that ethernet-equipped power adapter comes standard with the $1,699 and $1,899 models. It’s not included with the $1,499 model, but you can select it as an option at the point of purchase—and yes, that means you’ll have to pay extra for it.
How fast is it?: The 24-inch iMac is the only Mac still using the M4 chip, so it’s not as fast as the other Macs, but it’s still got all the speed general consumers need, and it can even handle pro applications with no problem. However, the $1,499 model has only one fan inside its body, while the $1,699 and $1,899 models have two fans. That means the high-priced models do a better job of keeping the internals cool. The $1,499 model may need to slow down its performance on heavy-duty tasks in order to maintain a proper temperature.
Any other considerations? The iMac doesn’t represent particularly good value at its current price. A better buy is the MacBook Air, which offers a faster M5 chip with a 10-core CPU, 8-core GPU, 16GB of memory, and a 512GB SSD for $1,299/£1,299. By comparison, the iMac costs $1,499/£1,499 yet includes an older M4 chip with an 8-core CPU, 8-core GPU, the same 16GB of memory, and only a 256GB SSD. We feel that the iMac price is high compared to the specs on offer, but we do admire the design. We are holding out for a bigger screen. Apple is rumored to launch a M6 iMac in 2027.
Why we recommend the iMac (M4): The iMac was transformed when Apple introduced the redesigned 24-inch model in 2021, with major improvements to its design, display, and performance. If you’re buying one today, the $1,699/£1,699 model is the sweet spot, adding more ports, Touch ID, and Ethernet. We’d still love to see Apple revive the iMac Pro with a larger display, and sincerely hope one is in the pipeline. 

							
		
Which Mac is best for what you do?
In the table below you can find the best Mac for every use case we can think of. Find the Mac that is best for you and meets your needs below. 


WhoRecommended MacWhy

Big screen/pro use16-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro)Largest laptop display combined with outstanding battery life and workstation-class performance

 FAQ 


1.
What’s best, MacBook Air or MacBook Pro?
We address this question in detail in our comparison of the MacBook Air vs Pro. It’s really a question of price versus power. The Air is sufficient for most people’s needs, the Pro will give you that extra boost in terms of what the Mac is capable of.
Buying an entry-level MacBook Air for $1,299/£1,299 will get you an excellent Mac laptop. If you want to spend less than that you may be able to find a discounted MacBook Air – we round up the best MacBook Air deals regularly.
If you want a larger screen, the 15-inch MacBook Air is a great option that is a lot cheaper than the smaller 14-inch MacBook Pro. 
The price of the Pro and Max MacBook Pro models is high, but these models offer the kind of specs professional users, especially creatives, need, including support for more RAM, and more CPU and GPU cores. If you can afford to stretch to the Max you will get the ultimate Mac without a doubt, but you need to be willing to make a significant investment.
The choice between the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro is all down to the screen size. The 16-inch models are more expensive, but once you spec them out in such a way to be comparable the price difference is minor. The bigger difference is between the Pro and Max processors. Other than speed, MacBooks with Max processors can connect up to four external displays (three over Thunderbolt and one over HDMI), while since the M4 all models allow two external displays in addition to the laptop screen. (There are workarounds if you need to connect more screens).
There is now another Mac laptop to consider, the MacBook Neo lowers the price of ownership of a Mac laptop to $699/£699. If budget really is tight though, you might want to consider a discounted previous generation MacBook Air instead.





2.
Should I upgrade from my Intel Mac?
Yes. It’s time! We are now more than six years into Apple’s transition from Intel processors to its own silicon that includes CPU, GPU, and unified memory. The transition began with the introduction of the M1 in November 2020. Since June 2023 every Mac Apple sells uses Apple’s own chips rather than Intel processors.
If you’ve yet to upgrade your Intel Mac to one powered by Apple’s silicon what are you waiting for? If you are concerned that a must-have app doesn’t run on an M-series Mac, consider finding a new app because the performance gains are tremendous.
Another good reason to update your Intel Mac is that Intel chips will not be supported by Apple for much longer in terms of security updates. With the arrival of macOS Tahoe, the number of supported Intel Macs was fewer than ever, and when the next version of macOS – macOS Golden Gate – launches later in 2026 it will not support any Intel powered Macs. This doesn’t mean that in fall 2026 Intel Macs will be out in the cold, because Apple continues to support older versions of macOS with security updates for a couple more years, but, with only a few of the most recent Intel Macs supported by 2024’s Sequoia the days of Intel Macs are certainly numbered. Read: How long does Apple support Macs. 





3.
Where can I get the best price for a new Mac?
Apple rarely offers direct price cuts on new hardware, but resellers frequently do. Getting the best price on a new Mac requires knowing where to look and when to buy: 
Top U.S. Retailers:
Amazon: Often has the lowest prices, especially during events like Prime Day. For example, during the July 2026 Prime Day event, a 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro was available for $1,749, a $450 discount. Even outside of events, Amazon frequently undercuts Apple’s MSRP.
Best Buy: A reliable source for discounts and trade-in offers. In late 2025, Best Buy offered a massive $1,150 off an M2 Ultra Mac Studio.
B&H Photo: A well-regarded authorized reseller that often has competitive pricing on Macs.
Walmart: Known for exclusive deals on older models, like the M1 MacBook Air, which has been sold brand-new for just $599.
Top U.K. Retailers:
Amazon UK: Similar to the U.S., Amazon UK is a primary source for discounts.
KRCS: An Apple Premium Reseller that frequently offers good deals.
John Lewis & Currys: Reliable high-street retailers that often have competitive prices and good customer service.
If you’re looking for a great offer, visit our MacBook Pro deals, MacBook Air deals, iMac deals, Mac Studio deals, and Mac mini deals pages which are regularly updated.





4.
What specs do I really need for my Mac?
Chip: The specs you need depend on what you plan to do with your Mac. For everyday tasks such as web browsing, email, office apps and light photo editing, a standard M-series chip is more than sufficient. Apple’s latest entry-level desktop chip is the M6, available in the Mac mini, while other Macs still use M4 or M5-generation chips. 
If you regularly work with complex spreadsheets, large Photoshop files, audio projects, video editing or more demanding games, look at a Pro chip. The M5 Pro Mac mini, for example, offers up to an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU and up to 64GB unified memory.
For professional video production, 3D work, software development and other intensive workloads, a Max chip is more appropriate. The Mac Studio with M5 Max offers an 18-core CPU, up to a 40-core GPU and as much as 128GB unified memory. 
The M5 Ultra, with up to a 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU and 512GB unified memory, is aimed at the most extreme workloads, including VFX, scientific computing and running very large AI models locally.
GPU: One of the biggest differences between Apple’s chips is GPU performance. Standard M-series chips are easily sufficient for everyday graphics, casual gaming and light creative work. Pro chips add considerably more GPU power for video editing, graphics work, 3D applications and gaming. Max chips are designed for professional graphics, high-resolution video and demanding 3D workflows, while Ultra provides Apple’s highest GPU performance. The M5 Max offers up to 40 GPU cores, while the M5 Ultra doubles that to 80 GPU cores. Both also have Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core to speed up AI workloads.
RAM: Apple calls RAM Unified Memory. The MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB, which is probably the biggest drawback of that machine. Most Macs start with at least 16GB, which is plenty for everyday use, although we recommend choosing more if your budget allows because the memory cannot be upgraded later. 24GB or 32GB is a good choice for heavier multitasking, photo editing, podcasting, moderate video production and gaming. Developers and professional creative users may benefit from 48GB, 64GB or more. The new M5 Pro Mac mini can be configured with up to 64GB, M5 Max Mac Studio with up to 128GB, and M5 Ultra Mac Studio with an enormous 512GB.
Storage: Even with iCloud and external drives available, it can seem like you can never have enough storage inside your Mac. 256GB may be sufficient for basic web and office use, but it can fill up quickly. We recommend 512GB for most people who want to keep a Mac for several years, particularly if you store photos, games or media locally. For regular video or audio production, 1TB or more is preferable. Professional users may need several terabytes: the M5 Pro Mac mini can be configured with up to 8TB, while Mac Studio configurations go even higher. As with unified memory, internal Mac storage cannot be upgraded after purchase, so it is worth thinking about future requirements when ordering.
For more information to help you decide which Mac to buy see our Mac processor comparison where we compare Apple silicon and Intel. We also offer advice about how much storage, RAM, and cores in How much MacBook RAM, SSD, GPU, and CPU do you really need.





5.
When were the Macs last updated?
In August 2026 the Mac mini and Mac Studio were updated. 
In March 2026 the MacBook Pro and MacBook Air were updated, and the MacBook Neo was introduced.
The most recent iMac update was in October 2024.
The Mac Pro has been discontinued. 





Why you can trust Macworld’s advice
Macworld has been covering everything Apple related since our first issue which arrived alongside the original Mac in 1984. Nobody knows Apple better, except probably Apple, but the difference is that we are completely impartial. We are made up of a team of experts with decades of experiences with Macs and other Apple products, and between us we have reviewed every Apple product meaning we are uniquely positioned to provide buying advice.

title: 75% of US Adults Aren't Interested in a Foldable iPhone
content:
Three out of four U.S. adults say they have no interest in buying a foldable iPhone, according to a new survey from CNET.


CNET's survey was conducted online by YouGov between August 13 and 17, polling 2,605 U.S. adults. It found that 75% are not interested in an Apple foldable device, and those who are would not pay anywhere near the rumored $2,000+ price.

CNET noted that a quarter of respondents still expressing interest in the device is a notable proportion for what remains a niche product category.

iPhone 17. Gen Z was willing to spend the most, an average of $919, followed by millennials at $859, Gen X at $690, and Boomers at $572. That mismatch between expected pricing and what buyers actually want to pay highlights just how far a $2,000+ device will sit outside most people's budgets.

CNET found that 41% of U.S. adults are rethinking their upgrade plans because of anticipated price increases. Apple raised prices on most of its devices in June, citing the global memory shortage, though iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods prices were untouched at the time. The iPhone 18 Pro lineup is expected to cost more than its predecessor when it launches for the same reasons.

title: New Mac Mini Bumps Display Refresh Rates to 165Hz
content:
Apple's newly announced M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini models still support up to three external displays, but there's now support for higher refresh rates, according to Apple's published technical specifications.


Here's what's changed versus the M4 generation:

  
The M6 model runs two displays at up to 6K 60Hz or 4K 165Hz, up from 144Hz on M4, plus a third display at up to 5K 60Hz over Thunderbolt or 4K 60Hz over HDMI.

  
The M5 Pro model runs all three displays at up to 6K 60Hz or 4K 165Hz, up from 144Hz on the M4 Pro.

  
In a two-monitor setup, the M5 Pro model's second screen now supports 5K 120Hz or 4K 200Hz, whereas the M4 Pro listed 6K 60Hz or 4K 144Hz.

  
The M5 Pro model supports all three displays through one Thunderbolt port, while the M6 still supports two per port.

  
Single-display support is unchanged: Both chips support 8K 60Hz, 5K 120Hz, or 4K 240Hz.

As for port compatibility around the back, the M6 model has Thunderbolt 4 supporting DisplayPort 1.4, while the M5 Pro model has Thunderbolt 5 supporting DisplayPort 2.1.

title: How to upgrade your Mac mini without paying Apple’s sky high prices
content:
Macworld





The Mac mini boasts fast processors, and rivals even Apple’s most pro computers despite costing significantly less. However, as great as it is, there is a problem with the Mac mini—the at-purchase storage upgrades are pricey and after you buy one, it’s nearly impossible to upgrade its internal components. However, we’re here to help.
There are two basic Mac mini models: the latest M4/M5/M6 mini (5 inches square, 2 inches deep) and older M1/M2 mini (7.7 inches square, 1.4 inches deep). Here, we have rounded up the best hardware upgrades and accessories you can buy for either the old or newer models. Most of the M1/M2 tips work with the Apple Studio, too, as that remains the same size.
Apple doesn’t let you upgrade the Mac mini with inexpensive third-party components such as RAM or internal storage, and it prices its custom-build options at the very high end of affordability. With the earlier Mac mini Apple fixed the RAM to the processor and the SSD to the logic board so they couldn’t be swapped out after you buy one. The M4/M5/M6 mini is different with a detachable SSD but swapping this out is beyond most mere mortals.
Here we look at your best Mac mini upgrade options, adding: storage, memory, screen, speakers and microphone. If you want to jump straight to the reviews:
Hubs and docks for new Mac mini
Hubs and docks for Mac mini M2
Other Mac mini accessories

				
					

				
			Above: Inside the Mac mini M4/M5/M6. Although it looks easy, because Apple’s SSD controller is built into the chip, you can’t simply swap out its SSD with a part bought from Amazon or some computer store. If you can do this yourself you probably wouldn’t be reading this article!L0vertodream via X
Upgrading the Mac mini: Adding memory and storage
In our FAQ at the foot of this feature we go into more detail about the difficulties of upgrading the Mac mini’s internal components—as it is with most Macs. There are solutions that are quite messy, such as adding external storage. 

				
					

				
			Flexible but messy: A Mac mini with two external SSDs: a Plugable 1TB Thunderbolt 3 External SSD NVMe Drive and a CalDigit Tuff Nano (10Gbps USB-C). Thankfully there are less messy ways of adding fast storage to your Mac mini.
Foundry




Adding external storage
The simplest way to add storage to a Mac mini is the same as any other Mac: Connect an external hard drive or SSD using one of the Thunderbolt ports on the back of the computer. Even the slowest Solid-state drives (SSD) are faster than mechanical hard disk drives (HDD), but look out for speed differences—entry-level SSDs provide speeds of around 500MBps, while more advanced models can step up to 2,000MBps or even 6,000MBps. See SSD or HDD in the FAQs.
Another way to add inexpensive portable storage is via an SD or microSD card—once the go-to storage format for camera users but also a great format for cheap and portable backup and archive storage. Sadly, the Mac mini doesn’t have a card reader slot, so you’ll need to add one, such as this UGreen USB-C SD Card Reader for $15.
But these are admittedly ugly methods. You’ll have wires hanging out of the back of your Mac mini and a desk cluttered with drives. It’s neater to keep storage hidden inside. Apple won’t let you do it, but there are some great solutions that we have tested here.
Adding Internal storage
The best option is to get more internal storage in your Mac mini, but Apple’s custom-built pricing means upgrading a 256GB model to 1TB will cost you an extra $500, and 2TB will cost $1,000, while M5 Pro options cost even more: 4TB is $1,800 and 8TB will set you back a whopping $3,800.
If you can’t swing the prices for more storage or just decide later that you need more, there are hardware solutions that connect to the mini without messing up the footprint of the small computer. We’ve tested and reviewed these Mac mini storage accessories for you. The tested Mac mini hubs feature upgradeable and inexpensive internal storage plus a range of extra ports, supporting the NVMe form factors that resemble a stick of chewing gum.
Installing SSD into Mac mini hub or dock
Below we review the best Mac mini hubs and docks. Some include a hidden SSD enclosure where you can slot your own storage card with an included screwdriver and sometimes a thermal gel pad to transfer heat away from the drive and into the metal enclosure, preventing the SSD from overheating and suffering from thermal throttling.

				
					

				
			The Satechi CubeDock matched the latest Mac mini (M4/M5/M6) and hides its internal SSD slot under its base.
Simon Jary




For the M4/M5/M6 mini, there are SSD slots in the Ugreen 11-in-1 Mac mini Dock, Satechi CubeDock, Satechi Stand & Hub, and Orico MiniLink, reviewed below. Satechi has an M2 mini version of its Stand & Hub, and you can also choose the OWC ministack STX.
Installation is simple, with everything bar the SSD board itself included (screwdriver, screws, thermal gel pads). It’s a little fiddly but nothing to be worried about—if you can use a screwdriver, you can install the SSD board yourself.
SSD types: The docks and hubs we tested all take NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) M.2 SSDs, but check on the appropriate SSD size before investing in the SSD. Some take several lengths—for example 2230, 2242, 2260 and 2280—while others just fit the standard 2280. If that sounds scary, don’t worry as the 2280 is the most common SSD length.
SSD speeds: Note that the speed of the USB-C or Thunderbolt connection from the dock to the Mac mini will determine the data-transfer rate. A 10Gbps USB-C connection allows an SSD to achieve real-world transfer speeds of around 900 to 1,250 Megabytes per second (MBps). While 40Gbps Thunderbolt 4 or USB4 pipes have a theoretical maximum of 5,000MB/s, protocol overhead and enclosure translation typically cap your speeds at around 3,000MBps. An 80Gbps connection (such as Thunderbolt 5) supports real-world SSD speeds of up to 7,000MBps.
Upgrading the Mac mini: Adding ports and extra expansion
While the Mac mini has plenty of ports around the back, Apple includes just two USB-C to the front of the M4/M5/M6 mini, and did not bless the M2 Mac mini with any ports at the front at all. Alongside the SSD slots, all of the hubs and docks tested and reviewed here include an array of ports, including USB-A (missing from the M4 mini) and SD/MicroSD card readers (missing from the M2 and M4/M5/M6 Mac mini).
Thunderbolt, USB-C, Ethernet and HDMI are all included in the Mac mini. Having access to more Thunderbolt or USB-C is useful, especially if powered. Some docks feature faster Ethernet.
USB-A is the legacy port missing from the Mac mini M4, used mainly for flash drives, memory sticks and older devices. This has largely been replaced with USB-C, but having at least one at your disposal can be handy.
SD card readers are also missing from the Mac mini, and are an affordable way of adding ultra-portable storage cards, which are cheaper—but slower—than SSDs. You can buy a SanDisk memory card with 512GB of storage for under $100.
Another port-adding option is to buy yourself a Thunderbolt hub, such as the 40Gbps CalDigit Thunderbolt 4 Element Hub that features four 40Gbps Thunderbolt 4 ports (including one side-mounted upstream to the computer), four 10Gbps USB-A ports, and a power supply. The Element 5 Hub from the same company offers four Thunderbolt 5, two 10Gbps USB-C and three 10Gbps USB-A ports. We’ve tested the best Thunderbolt hubs and docks if you want even more ports than that. Granted, they won’t be as neat as the dedicated Mac mini docks and hubs reviewed here, but there are tons of options out there.
Best Mac mini hubs and docks
The criteria we used for the products reviewed below was that they had to fit the Mac mini and connect to it without ruining the Apple aesthetic or the Mac mini’s compact footprint. We tested the following docks and hubs with the Apple Mac mini (M4/M5/M6 models).

			

				
					

				
								
Pros
Fits Mac mini M4/M5/M6
Four Thunderbolt 5 ports
Built-in NVMe SSD slot
Two USB-C ports
Two USB-A ports
SD and MicroSD card readers
2.5Gb Ethernet

 FAQ 


1.
Can you upgrade the Mac mini hard drive?
It is possible to swap out the internal SSD on the latest Mac mini models (M4/M5/M6) but you’ll need to be very tech-savvy. You have to carefully pry open the bottom cover, remove the internal fan, swap the SSD module using Torx bits, and use a second Mac via DFU mode to restore the operating system. Note that opening the chassis voids your Apple warranty and risks damaging delicate internal connectors. Instead, we recommend you look at the add-on solutions reviewed here. 
Apple soldered the solid-state drive (SSD) directly onto the logic board of the older M1/M2Mac mini when you chose the capacity at the point of purchase. While it is not possible to later upgrade the drive, you can add extra SSDs or hard-disk drives (HDD) via accessories.





2.
Can you upgrade the Mac mini memory?
Apple builds the RAM directly as part of the processor of the Mac mini (unified memory architecture) when you choose the amount of memory at the point of purchase. It is not possible to later upgrade the RAM, so you must choose the most you are likely to need when buying the computer.





3.
SSD or HDD?
Solid-state drives (SSD) have no moving parts. Data is stored on interconnected flash memory microchips, which allows for data to be pulled from many different places at once and significantly increases memory read speeds. Hard disk drives (HDD) rely on spinning metal disks to read and write data.
Most of the solutions reviewed here are focused on the faster NVMe type of SSD that speed up boot times, improve the responsiveness of your programs, and generally make your computer feel faster. However, you’ll pay more money for the same storage capacity on SSDs as HDDs. SSDs cost more per gigabyte than mechanical HDDs and aren’t often available in ultra-high capacities. Even as prices of SSDs continue to drop, HDDs will always be cheaper.





4.
Upgrading the Mac mini: Adding faster ethernet
One of the build-to-order options offered by Apple is to upgrade the Mac mini’s ethernet from 1 Gigabit to 10 Gigabit (an extra $100). As with the RAM and storage, once you’ve picked your Ethernet speed, there’s no way to upgrade the internal connector later. But you can buy adapters quite cheaply. Cable Matters sells a 10G Ethernet Adapter for around $89 if you suddenly need faster network access after you’ve purchased your Mac mini. Ugreen has 2.5GbE and 5GbE adapters that connect to one of your Mac’s USB-C or Thunderbolt ports.

title: Apple Car Key Support Coming to Xiaomi Auto Vehicles
content:
Apple's Car Keys feature appears to be coming to supported vehicles made by Chinese maker Xiaomi Auto, based on code changes discovered by MacRumors in Apple's Wallet app backend.


Code spotted in the third developer beta of iOS 27 back in July revealed that Apple was preparing Car Keys support for Xiaomi, so this latest change suggest support is imminent. 

The Chinese electronics maker has expanded into EVs with models like the SU7 sedan and YU7 SUV. Car key support would be one of the company's first tie-ins with Apple's ecosystem, despite Xiaomi being a major Apple rival in the smartphone market.

Car Keys allows an iPhone or Apple Watch with NFC capabilities to unlock a vehicle through the Wallet app. A digital version of a car key is stored in Wallet, and unlocking can be done simply by holding an Apple Watch or ‌iPhone‌ near a compatible vehicle's NFC reader.

What can be done with Car Keys may vary by car manufacturer, but at a minimum, Car Keys can be used to unlock your car, lock your car, and start your car, which are the features available with a physical key.

title: iOS 27 has an intriguing new Drawing app for scribbling Messages
content:
Macworld





You’ve been able to send little handwritten doodles through iMessages for a long time now. There’s Digital Touch, which lets you create an animated recreation of your little doodles, and you can also rotate the phone to landscape view in the message window to access the drawing feature and use your finger to scribble a message or jot down a doodle. 
In iOS 27, Apple has removed that second option, instead adding a new Drawing app that you access via the (+) button, as you would with other iMessage apps. The concept is similar, but it’s a little more sophisticated in that you have access to all the standard iOS drawing pens and tools.
Why would Apple make this change? It could be that the old method was a little hard to find, as it required both rotating your iPhone and knowing what the small unlabeled button did. But it might also have something to do with a certain folding iPhone expected to debut around the same time as iOS 27.
Some are speculating that the replacement of the old drawing/handwriting feature with a dedicated Drawing app is related to the upcoming iPhone Ultra folding phone, since that Phone will have a larger canvas that’s more suited for drawing. That may be true, but I think the explanation is simpler: The old feature dates all the way back to iOS 12, and was sort of hard to find. Now that Apple has a standard drawing toolbar and features used across Markup, Notes, and other apps, it makes sense to replace the old handwriting tool with something that will match what Apple does through the rest of the operating system.
Whatever the reason, this is how it works.
How to send a drawing to someone in Messages
You’ll find the new Drawing app in the (+) menu to the left of the text entry bar, where all the iMessages apps live.
Start a new message.
Tap the (+) button on the left.
Select Drawing (you may have to scroll the list).
Doodle something. Tap the drawing tools at the bottom to change the tool, its options, or the colors.
Tap the checkbox in the upper right, and your doodle will be attached to your next message as an image.
Compose the rest of your message and hit send.

title: M5 vs. M6 Chip Buyer's Guide: How Much Better Really Is M6?
content:
Apple yesterday announced the M6, its first chip built using a 2nm process and the first Apple silicon design to use three different CPU core types, but how does it compare to the M5?


Compared to the M5 chip that Apple launched in October 2025, the M6 delivers:


 
Up to 1.2x faster multithreaded CPU performance.

 
Nearly 30% higher peak GPU compute for AI.

 
Up to 2x peak Neural Engine compute.

 
50% higher geometry rates for complex graphics.

 
10% higher unified memory bandwidth.



Mac mini figures against the M4 and M1 models:


Up to 13.5x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio versus ‌M1‌, and up to 4.8x faster versus the M4.

Up to 2.3x faster spreadsheet calculations in Microsoft Excel versus ‌M1‌, and up to 1.5x faster versus the M4.

Up to 2x faster gaming performance with ray tracing in "Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition" versus the M4.



The most significant architectural change is in the CPU. The M5 splits its ten cores into performance and efficiency groups, which is an arrangement Apple silicon has used since the ‌M1‌. The M6 adds a third tier called "super cores," which handle single-threaded workloads and which Apple says give the chip the world's fastest single-threaded performance.

The performance cores join them for heavier multithreaded work, while the efficiency cores take background tasks. The second major change is the Neural Engine, which is now doubled, with system frameworks able to use both engines at once so apps see faster model execution without any work from developers required. Other hardware changes compared to the M5 include:



Apple M5 Chip (2025)
Apple M6 Chip (2026)


Made with TSMC's third-generation 3nm process (N3P)
Made with TSMC's first-generation 2nm process (N2)


FinFET transistors
Gate-all-around nanosheet transistors


10-core CPU with 4 performance cores and 6 efficiency cores
12-core CPU with 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores



Super cores dedicated to single-threaded workloads


16-core Neural Engine
Dual 16-core Neural Engine that system frameworks can run simultaneously


10-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in every core
12-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in every core


Enhanced shader cores
Updated shader core architecture


Second-generation dynamic caching
Third-generation dynamic caching


153 GB/s unified memory bandwidth
170 GB/s unified memory bandwidth




The move to a 2nm process is a significant technical change. Apple chips have used FinFET transistors for years, but the M6's N2 process uses a newer design with gate-all-around nanosheet transistors. This means that the transistor's gate wraps around the channel on every side, giving it better control and reducing power leakage at tiny sizes.

TSMC says N2 can offer 10–15% more speed at the same power, or 25–30% lower power use at the same speed, compared with its N3E process. But the M5 uses the newer N3P process, not N3E, so the actual M5-to-M6 improvement is likely to be smaller than those figures suggest.

The M6 is a broad but fairly modest upgrade. It improves the CPU, GPU, Neural Engine, and memory bandwidth, rather than delivering a dramatic gain in one area. The M5's biggest leap was in AI-focused GPU performance, thanks to Neural Accelerators built into each GPU core. The M6's reported 1.2× multithreaded CPU gain and 10% increase in memory bandwidth are good refinements rather than step-changes.

Single-threaded performance is the main exception. Some tasks cannot be split across many CPU cores, including code compilation, file indexing, image editing, and parts of agentic AI workflows. These tasks depend heavily on the speed of one core, and the M6's new "super cores" are designed to improve that directly. A doubled Neural Engine should also help with local AI models, while the larger GPU can process prompts faster.

For everyday work and general responsiveness, the difference will probably be difficult to notice. The M5 already has more than enough performance for normal use, so there is little general-purpose reason to upgrade from an M5 to an M6.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported in July that Apple has no plans to release "M6 Pro," "M6 Max," or "M6 Ultra" chips, having decided to accelerate development of the AI-optimized M7 generation. The new Mac mini illustrates this point, since its higher-specification configuration uses the M5 Pro. That makes the M6 the first of its kind to not have higher-end variants, and it means the M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra remain the chips to buy if you need anything more than base-tier performance. 

The dual Neural Engine and 2nm process give the M6 headroom for on-device AI tools that grow more demanding, but the M7 is expected in the first half of 2027 with neural processing upgrades that prompted Apple to cut the M6 lineup short. If your workloads are AI-heavy enough that the M6's gains matter to you, the chip designed for exactly that is less than a year away.

new Mac mini, which starts at $899 and ships on September 22. M6 versions of the MacBook Pro and iMac are expected to be announced in October. The M5 chip remains available in the 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌, the latest iPad Pro, and the Apple Vision Pro, with M5 Pro and M5 Max in the higher-end ‌MacBook Pro‌ models and M5 Max and M5 Ultra in the new Mac Studio.

title: Mac-ify your iPad with these 10 must-have accessories
content:
Macworld





Every year, iPadOS borrows a couple of desktop features, bringing Apple’s tablet closer to the Mac. At this point, some professionals have effectively replaced their MacBooks with iPads, simplifying their setups and making them more portable. An iPad on its own, however, is insufficient to mimic a MacBook. One cannot practically type long-form text using the virtual keyboard or rely exclusively on touch controls for daily tasks. Fortunately, with just a few accessories, you can completely transform your iPad experience and upgrade it to a MacBook-like computer.
Keyboard
A keyboard is the most essential productivity accessory you can get for your iPad. Not only does it make typing more intuitive, but it also unlocks advanced keyboard shortcuts across apps—accelerating your workflows in the process. Luckily, iPadOS supports a wide range of keyboards, including most standard Bluetooth ones. Apple sells the Magic Keyboard for various iPad models, which doubles as a stand and protective case. It also includes an embedded trackpad, essentially turning your iPad into a laptop. For something more budget-friendly, you can’t go wrong with the Logitech Keys-to-Go Bluetooth Keyboard. It is designed specifically for Apple products, supports multi-device connections, and features a portable design.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Mouse
Like keyboards, iPadOS supports most Bluetooth mice and trackpads, and will show a dedicated cursor when using one. This spares you from touching the display for interacting with on-screen elements and replicates the Mac experience. For a reliable, ergonomic mouse, go with the Logitech MX Master 4. It features a comfortable build and long battery life, making it suitable for long work hours. If you’d rather spend less, you can buy a Microsoft-branded Bluetooth mouse for a fraction of the price. It may not offer as many customization options or perks as certain alternatives, but it’ll reliably get the job done.
External display
iPadOS is natively compatible with external monitors, letting you get work done on larger displays. M-series iPads support secondary workspaces, allowing you to simultaneously interact with different windows on the built-in screen and external one. Less powerful iPad models limit external display support to screen mirroring, which is still decent for those seeking a wider canvas. For a dependable option, you may want to consider the Dell 27 Monitor S2725QC. It features a 4K resolution, USB-C connectivity, 120Hz refresh rate, and more. Planning to work on the go? Go with the Asus ZenScreen 15.6 Inch Portable Monitor instead. It may not be as advanced, but it’s certainly sufficient for mobile setups.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




USB-C dongle
iPads only offer a single USB-C port, and that can limit the peripherals you can connect to them—especially during charging sessions. Fortunately, you can add more ports to your iPad by connecting a dongle. There are endless options offered by a wide range of brands, featuring various port types and price ranges that cater to all sorts of customers. Some solid dongles include those from Anker, Acer, and Ugreen. Ensure your iPad model is compatible with your selection before completing your purchase.
Docking Station
If you’re not a big fan of dangling dongles, you could opt for a docking station instead. Several excellent brands offer dedicated stands that incorporate additional ports for your iPad. They are ideal for stable setups and will maintain your desk’s minimalistic, clutter-free look. The Satechi 6-in-1 USB-C Stand Hub and Anker 551 USB-C Hub with Foldable Stand will both transform your iPad into a serious workstation.
Stand
If your setup is primarily wireless, you could still get a stand without any of the extra ports. This allows you to fix your iPad at a comfortable viewing angle and makes using standalone Bluetooth keyboards and mice more practical. Some of the popular stands include those from Moft, Ugreen, and Lisen.
External storage
While wireless cloud solutions tend to be more convenient, certain fields limit us to local file storage and transfer. The iPad supports hard drives and USB sticks, letting you quickly browse and move data using the built-in Files app. The WD 2TB My Passport is a high-end option for those handling large files. Those with more basic needs can safely go with the Sandisk 512GB Ultra Dual Drive Go Flash Drive.
Game controller
If you’re using your iPad as a MacBook replacement, you’ll want to prepare for gaming sessions. Like macOS, iPadOS fully supports Sony DualSense, Xbox, and MFi controllers, allowing you to wirelessly pair and customize them as needed.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Speaker
Laptops are often used for consuming media, including music while working and movie streaming when away from a TV. If you’re planning to use an iPad as your main computer, you’ll want to invest in some audio output accessories. For private listening, you’ve got the Beats Studio Buds +, Sony WH-CH720N, and Bose QuietComfort Ultra Gen 2. Otherwise, you could get some loud speakers, like the Bose Lifestyle Ultra, Sonos Era 100, or JBL Charge 6.
Microphone
With the digital content creation boom, a professional microphone has become a must-have accessory for many iPad users. Whether you’re podcasting, attending virtual conferences, or starting an ASMR YouTube channel, you’ll need something crisper-sounding than your iPad’s built-in mics. iPadOS supports both wired and wireless microphones, so your options are plentiful. Some of the best microphones include the Rode Wireless Go Gen 3, Shure MV7+, and DJI Mic Mini.

				
					

				
			
Foundry
